subject: Sliding versus hinged wardrobe doors
hook: Sliding or hinged wardrobe doors? Five questions will settle it faster than any showroom.
ig:
Sliding or hinged wardrobe doors? Five questions will settle it faster than any showroom.

1. How much floor is in front? A hinged door needs roughly its own width of clear space to swing. Bed close to the wardrobe? Sliding is usually the answer.

2. Do you need to see everything at once? Hinged doors open the full width. Sliding doors always leave one section covered.

3. What is going inside? Drawers behind sliding doors have to be positioned to clear the overlap. Hinged doors give you far more freedom.

4. Is the room level? Sliding doors run on tracks that must be set dead level, which takes more care in older houses.

5. What look are you after? Sliding gives large, calm panels. Hinged gives rhythm and lets handles become a feature.

Neither is better in every room. The right fitted wardrobe is the one that suits your floor space and the way you get dressed.

Save this for when you are deciding, and see our fitted wardrobes via the link in bio.
fb:
Sliding or hinged? It is the first question almost everyone asks about fitted wardrobes, and the honest answer is: it depends on your room.

If the bed is close to the wardrobe, sliding doors save the swing space. If you want to see everything at once and fit drawers anywhere you like, hinged doors win. Uneven floors and ceilings can be handled either way, but sliding tracks need a bit more care to set level.
